fullPassage: How does music improve cognition? Music listening and especially music-making is stimulating many psychological functions; however, core functions addressed by musical activities are executive functions. These include attention, working memory, planning, and motor control, all relying on networks predominantly located in the frontal cortex. Musical engagement was found to increase grey matter density in frontal brain areas involved in controlling the practised task. Further evidence that musical practice involves the frontal cortex in elderly adults has been provided by Sluming et al. These authors demonstrated that musicians who practise beyond 60 years of age show less or no degeneration of grey matter density in the frontal cortex. Thus, practising a musical instrument seems to prevent degeneration of the frontal cortex and deterioration of the above-mentioned executive functions. Results of Verghese et al. hint in the same direction, demonstrating that Alzheimer’s dementia is less common in the elderly who are regularly involved in musical activities.

❌ ② The Hidden Costs of Learning an Instrument(악기 학습의 숨은 대가): 대가·단점은 본문에 없어요.

❌ ③ Dementia: A Disease Beyond Any Cure(치매: 어떤 치료로도 고칠 수 없는 병): 글은 음악의 보호 효과를 말하므로 반대 분위기예요.
det.tip: 제목은 글의 핵심(음악=뇌 보호)을 비유로 압축한 선지가 유력해요.

questions.passage: How does music improve cognition? Music listening and especially music-making is stimulating many psychological functions; however, core functions addressed by musical activities are executive functions. These include attention, working memory, planning, and motor control, all relying on networks predominantly located in the frontal cortex. Musical engagement was found to increase grey matter density in frontal brain areas involved in controlling the practised task. Further evidence that musical practice involves the frontal cortex in elderly adults has been provided by Sluming et al. These authors demonstrated that musicians who practise beyond 60 years of age show less or no degeneration of grey matter density in the frontal cortex. Thus, practising a musical instrument seems to prevent degeneration of the frontal cortex and deterioration of the above-mentioned executive functions. Results of Verghese et al. <u>hint in the same direction</u>, demonstrating that Alzheimer’s dementia is less common in the elderly who are regularly involved in musical activities.
questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 hint in the same direction이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 함축: 앞선 연구들과 같은 결론(음악의 보호 효과)을 가리킨다
det.analysis:
✅ ② 앞선 연구들과 같은 결론을 뒷받침한다: Verghese 등의 결과가 Sluming 등의 앞선 연구와 '같은 방향'을 가리킨다는 뜻이에요. 뒤의 '치매가 덜 흔함'이 앞의 보호 효과와 일치해요.

❌ ① 서로 반대되는 결과: same direction(같은 방향)과 정반대예요.

❌ ③ 연구 방향을 바꾸어야 한다: 본문에 없는 내용이에요.

❌ ④ 음악이 치매의 원인: 음악은 치매를 '줄인다'고 했으므로 반대예요.
det.tip: in the same direction: (앞 연구와) 같은 방향으로 = 같은 결론을 뒷받침

ch: 연구 방향을 완전히 바꾸어야 함을 보여 준다

questions.stem: 위 글의 밑줄 친 These가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① 실행 기능: 바로 앞 문장에서 핵심 기능이 executive functions(실행 기능)라고 했고, These include attention, working memory ~로 그 구체 항목을 열거하고 있어요.

❌ ② 심리적 기능 전체: 음악이 자극하는 넓은 범위이지만, These가 가리키는 것은 그중 '핵심'인 실행 기능이에요.

❌ ③ 전두엽 피질의 신경망: These 뒤에 나오는 대상(의존처)이지 These 자체가 아니에요.

❌ ④ 음악 활동의 종류: 열거된 항목(주의·기억 등)과 맞지 않아요.
det.tip: These include ~: 바로 앞의 명사(executive functions)를 받아 항목을 나열해요.
